title: He asked for more time…
paragraphs:
He asked for more time…
—and God stopped the sun.
Let that sit on your chest for a second.

Because we don’t struggle with time…
we struggle with what we’ve done inside the time we were given.
And that’s where the tension begins.

You’ve prayed before.
But not like that.

Not bold.
Not dangerous.
Not the kind of prayer that risks disappointment.
Because deep down, there’s a voice whispering—
“After what you’ve done… God won’t move for you.”
So you settle.

Small prayers.
Safe words.
Religious routine.
While your real battles stay untouched.
Unspoken.
Unhealed.

You show up to church, but your heart is carrying hidden defeat.
You worship, but there’s a quiet shame gripping your soul.
You say “God is good,” but inside you’re thinking—
“Not to me. Not anymore.”
And here’s the raw truth most people won’t say out loud:

We don’t just fear failure…
we fear that our failure has disqualified us.
So we shrink.

We stop asking boldly.
We stop believing deeply.
We stop expecting anything supernatural.
But Joshua didn’t.
He stood in the middle of war—dust in his lungs, blood on the ground, enemies closing in—and he dared to ask for the impossible.

“Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon.”
—Joshua 10:12
That’s not a quiet prayer.
That’s not a safe prayer.
That’s a man who believed God was still listening—even in chaos.
And Scripture says:

“The sun stopped in the midst of heaven and did not hurry to set for about a whole day. There has been no day like it before or since, when the Lord heeded the voice of a man, for the Lord fought for Israel.”
—Joshua 10:13–14
Read that again.
The Lord listened.
Not because Joshua was perfect.
But because Joshua trusted.
Now don’t miss this.

This moment was not about Joshua’s greatness.
It was about God’s faithfulness to His covenant.
And here’s where it confronts us.

Some scholars interpret this event as a literal cosmic miracle—God suspending the natural order. Others suggest it could describe prolonged daylight through divine intervention in ways we don’t fully understand.
But all agree on this:
God responded.
God fought.
God moved.
And the real question is not, “Can God stop the sun?”
The real question is—
Why have we stopped believing He can move in our lives?
Because shame is loud.

It reminds you of every failure.
Every hidden sin.
Every compromise you thought no one saw.
And slowly, you start believing the lie:
“I’m not the kind of person God answers anymore.”
But that’s where the Gospel explodes into the story.
Because Joshua points forward to Someone greater.
Jesus Christ.

Joshua asked for the sun to stand still…
but Jesus stepped into our darkness and defeated it completely.
You see, our biggest problem is not lack of time.
It’s sin.

Sin that separates us from God.
Sin that no amount of effort can erase.
Sin that leaves us guilty, exposed, and spiritually dead.

“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
—Romans 3:23
That’s all of us.
No exceptions.
But God didn’t leave us there.

“God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
—Romans 5:8
Jesus didn’t wait for you to clean yourself up.
He stepped into your mess.
He carried your sin.
He took your shame.

On the cross, Jesus absorbed the judgment we deserved.
And three days later, He rose—proving that sin, death, and hell don’t get the final word.
That’s not religion.
That’s rescue.
That’s grace.
And here’s the part that will break every lie shame has been telling you:

Because of Jesus…
you are not disqualified.
You are invited.

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
—1 John 1:9
Faithful.

Not hesitant.
Not reluctant.
Faithful.
So the reason you can pray boldly today is not because you’ve been perfect.
It’s because Jesus already paid for your imperfection.
Let that hit you.
The cross didn’t just forgive your past.
It restored your access.
Hebrews says:

“Let us then with confidence draw near to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.”
—Hebrews 4:16
Confidence.

Not shame.
Not hiding.
Not shrinking.
Confidence.
So what battle are you standing in right now?
Where have you already accepted defeat?
Where did you stop asking because you felt unworthy?
Listen carefully—

God is not intimidated by your situation.
And He is not repelled by your repentance.
He responds to hearts that come back.
Not perfect hearts.
Surrendered ones.
This is your moment.
Not to perform.
Not to pretend.
But to return.

To drop the mask.
To confess what’s real.
To stop negotiating with sin and start surrendering to Jesus.

Because the same God who commanded the sun…
is calling your name.
Right now.

Not tomorrow.
Not when you “feel ready.”
Now.
So pray.

Not small.
Not safe.
Pray like someone who knows Jesus already opened the way.
Say it plainly:
“Lord, I’ve been hiding. Forgive me. Cleanse me. Take my shame. Teach me to trust You again.”
And then stand.
Not in your strength.
But in His grace.
Let this be your moment of surrender.
